Q779.L1t: Chinglish is the term for English as influenced by Chinese vocabulary and grammar, and it often appears on public signs in China.
Q779.L2t: Radtke, a multimedia designer, has collected over 5,000 examples of Chinglish on his website and published two books about it.
Q779.L3t: Radtke argues that there is not just one standard English, and points out that millions of people already use Chinglish to communicate with one another.
Q779.L4t: Radtke holds that Chinglish is a real variety of English, used by millions of people to communicate, rather than a mere mistake.
Q779.L2f: Radtke began collecting Chinglish examples in 2012 after he moved to Beijing, and he has published a single book on the subject.
Q779.L3f: Radtke says that Chinglish exists mainly as entertainment, and that its main purpose is to give foreign visitors something to laugh at.
Q779.L4f: Radtke agrees that Chinglish was invented to amuse foreign tourists.

Q844.L1t: Sleep problems are common, and many habits during the day and evening can affect how well a person sleeps at night.
Q844.L2t: The advice says that when you cannot fall asleep within 20 minutes, you should get up and avoid bright light until you feel sleepy.
Q844.L3t: The advice says that if you cannot sleep you should get up and do something boring until you feel sleepy, because this helps you fall asleep.
Q844.L4t: Doing something dull, such as reading an uninteresting story, can help you fall asleep at night.
Q844.L2f: The advice says that a nap of several hours taken in the evening will make you more tired at bedtime.
Q844.L3f: The advice says that any exercise, whether done in the morning or just before bed, will always help you fall asleep faster.
Q844.L4f: Taking some exercise is what can help you fall asleep at night, whatever time you do it.

Q786.L1t: The letter is written as a humorous piece in which an alien visitor describes ordinary human life in an odd, unfamiliar way.
Q786.L2t: In the letter, the Martian describes people leaving big boxes, riding in small boxes on wheels, and going to very large tall boxes.
Q786.L3t: The Martian ends the letter by thanking the earthmen for the chance to get to know them, after saying he enjoyed his stay on an interesting, unusual planet.
Q786.L4t: The Martian feels that his stay on our unusual planet has been an interesting experience.
Q786.L2f: In the letter, the Martian says he found the tiny glowing boxes at the football game and was puzzled by them.
Q786.L3f: The Martian says he sat and watched the tiny glowing boxes in the big boxes, and that they were actual moving pictures to him, not television sets.
Q786.L4f: The Martian thinks the tiny glowing boxes are moving pictures.
